topic: How do on-board storage constraints influence payload power allocation between immediate and time-tagged service prioritization?
response: On-board storage constraints limit the amount of data packets that can be stored before operation begins. Immediate service prioritization allows for on-board memory to be directly utilized, while time-tagged services must account for pre-operation storage limitations. This constraint influences payload power allocation by dictating how much data needs to be transmitted and stored at specific times.
reference_context: The text mentions an on-board memory buffer (bs) with a size of bs. It also states that the size of data packets uploaded on satellites cannot exceed bs. This directly impacts the payload power allocation between immediate and time-tagged services.
